_comment: The blast-radius ledger: what a change to the foundation invalidated, and how it was cleared.
一份台账，不是一张许可名单。每条记录只回答一件事：这次层 S 的改动动了哪些结论、逐条怎么清的。
`entries` is append-only, like `docs/sphinx/source/foundation-log.rst`: a row is never deleted or
softened. An empty ledger is the honest starting state -- it does not mean nothing ever changed, it
means nothing has been cleared through this mechanism yet.
How `.github/project/blast_gate.py` uses it:
* a changed file under `include/foc/`, `src/` or the SIL instruments triggers a ledger entry when at
least `fan_in_threshold` claim rows rest on it, or when it is listed in `watched`;
* the affected set is RECOMPUTED from `claim-basis.json` (transitive closure) and never taken from
the entry -- a hand-written radius that disagrees with the graph is the failure mode;
* every affected row needs a verdict: `holds` (with a reason), `retest` (with the new number and its
evidence) or `refuted` (with the README level it was downgraded to);
* a `watched` instrument that no claim row mentions must carry `hand_rerun`, because an entry that
adjudicates nothing is an empty ritual;
* only entries touched by the current diff get their radius re-checked: an old entry's radius grows as
the graph grows, and re-litigating it on every later commit would punish the wrong commit.
`watched` is a ratchet: each entry is a layer-S instrument whose change re-bases every SIL number, so
adding one requires a reason in the same commit. Removing one when the file is gone is required, not
optional -- the gate refuses a watch whose file no longer exists.
Known boundary, stated rather than hidden: the graph's edges are compile edges and quoted identifiers, so
it sees a changed implementation and cannot see changed *semantics* behind an unchanged signature. Those
changes are seeded by hand and marked `manual_seed` in the entry.
Known boundary, second half: the trigger needs a diff. In a shallow CI checkout the default base yields
nothing to inspect, and the gate says so in its own output instead of reporting a clean pass as if the
trigger had been checked.

Known limit, found by the first entry: the trigger keys on fan-out as well as fan-in, because `motor.hpp` consumes seventeen modules and is consumed by one -- but the RADIUS is still the fan-in closure, so a fan-out-triggered change can name very few rows (the first entry settled exactly one). That is not a bug in the closure: the graph records 'this claim rests on that module', and a row whose numbers merely travel *through* a file it never names is invisible here. The entry's `what_changed` sentence is what carries that half, which is why it is not optional.

watched.test_package/test/unit/sil_abc_plant.hpp: the phase-variable plant: the second model every dq number is cross-checked against (M-01)
watched.test_package/test/unit/sil_bench.hpp: the scenario harness every SIL number is measured through
watched.test_package/test/unit/sil_discrete_inve: the switching-level inverter: dead-time, forward-drop and loss numbers come from it
watched.test_package/test/unit/sil_hall_sensor.h: the hall rig: the mount-error numbers for hall decoding and six-step commutation
watched.test_package/test/unit/sil_metrics.hpp: how a step is scored (rise, overshoot, settling): a change re-bases every metric claim
watched.test_package/test/unit/sil_plant_hal.hpp: the HAL that couples the plant to `Motor`, so a change moves every closed-loop number
watched.test_package/test/unit/sil_pmsm_plant.hp: the dq plant, the instrument under M-01
watched.test_package/test/unit/sil_speed_step_ca: the speed-step scenario shared by the loop claims
watched.test_package/test/unit/sil_switching_rig: the duty-replay rig used wherever a real PWM train is needed

entries.what_changed: `Motor` gained a breakaway sequence (`begin_stall_start()`, the three read-outs, and a tick branch that derives `iq` from it while its phase is `Ramping`), and the same capability reached the C surface (`foc_motor_begin_stall_start` / `_get_` / `_cancel_`). Nothing else about the loop moved.

the row did not exist when B-01 was written; it is inside this entry's radius because `core/trace.hpp` names `motor/motor.hpp` as its basis, so every reader of the trace inherits the loop's seeds. `trace_parse.hpp` includes `trace.hpp` and `types.hpp` only -- it neither includes nor calls the loop, so the breakaway branch cannot reach it. measured on this tree: `test_trace_parse` 7/7

new in this batch, and it sits in the radius because its basis names `api/foc_api.h`, which is one of this entry's seeds -- a protocol reader of the C surface inherits whatever the C surface inherits. The breakaway branch cannot reach it: it calls `foc_motor_get_status`, `foc_get_state`, `foc_motor_trace_size` and `foc_motor_trace_dropped`, and none of them enters the stall sequence. measured on this tree: `test_register_map` 3/3, including a real motor read that agrees with the C entry point bit for bit

entries.what_changed: Two layer-S edits made to ship F45 and F52. (1) `Motor::apply_params()` gained the definition it never had: it has been declared and documented since 0.1.0, `machine_params.hpp` describes the hook in prose, and `has_apply_params_v` exists to find it -- but there was no definition anywhere in the tree, so it could not link. Nothing called it, which is why nothing noticed; the first caller was the F45 example. (2) `core::MachineMap` gained `covers()` so that the clamp it has always performed is askable instead of silent; `at()` is untouched. `core/trace_parse.hpp` is new and reads `TraceSample` only. `core/machine_map.hpp` is not a seed by the fan-in rule -- it is listed because a layer-S edit was made to it and an entry that skips the file it edited is not a ledger.

affected.why: `apply_params()` forwards to the policies and stores nothing -- `config_` is not touched -- so the numbers the loop records are unchanged, and the new definition cannot run on any path that existed before because no caller could link to it. measured on this tree: `test_trace` 7/7

a new row, measured on the post-change tree rather than assumed: the header reads `TraceSample` and holds no state between calls, so neither edit can reach it. `test_trace_parse` 7/7, including the 32-bit wrap case and the injected interior gap

`covers()` is a new member: `at()`, `valid()`, `read_document()` and `write_document()` are byte-identical, and the text row's claim is about the round trip through those. measured on this tree: `test_machine_map` 6/6, `test_machine_map_text` 7/7 -- the L3 round-trip numbers did not move
